storage: Four private integer scratch arrays use newByteArray# (8*n), scalar initialization and readInt64Array#/writeInt64Array#. Node, Kind and descendant arrays remain boxed.
Construction-time value demand is retained before the write action. Bounds checks, lazy index expressions and Magic.lazy state actions remain.
The boxed array slot was also eight bytes, holding a pointer; total initial 0/-1 values can be shared. This is not a halving of slot payload or one saved initial box per slot.
limits: Some reads still rebox Int64; colour and visited comparisons consume scalars directly.
Original boxed reads can return existing boxes without allocation. Eight-byte scalar slots do not halve the old eight-byte pointer slots.
Private visibility/inlining changes confound attribution solely to storage.
Only final saved O2 Core; no separately retained O0 Core. No complete allocation/PAP/GC/error-path ledger.
No whole-program allocation or timing claim.
